title: Homeowner Identity Identification Through Account Registration
description: During account registration, the homeowner's personally identifiable information (PII) is collected and stored, making them identifiable to the system and potentially to third parties if data is breached or shared.
assumptions: Account registration requires personal information collection and storage.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Camera/Sensor Data
description: Video and sensor data collected from enrolled cameras and sensors could be accessed or disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper data sharing practices.
assumptions: Camera/sensor data contains sensitive information about home occupants and activities.

title: Excessive Data Collection During Device Enrollment
description: The device enrollment process may collect more personal and environmental data than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Enrollment process may request permissions or data beyond what is strictly needed for basic functionality.

title: Linkability of Homeowner Data Across Services
description: Data collected during account registration and device enrollment could be linked to other data sources (e.g., other smart home services, online accounts), creating a comprehensive profile of the homeowner.
assumptions: Homeowner may use multiple interconnected services that share data.

title: Homeowner Account Usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate the homeowner by compromising account credentials, gaining unauthorized access to the home hub and all enrolled devices.
assumptions: Account credentials may be vulnerable to phishing, credential stuffing, or other attacks.

title: Guest access code linked to identity
description: The Home Hub may log guest access code entries and link them to guest identity or other data, enabling correlation of access events with specific individuals.

title: Access code disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The temporary access code may be visible to others, logged insecurely, or transmitted in a way that allows unauthorized parties to observe or intercept it.

title: Unauthorized use of access code
description: If the temporary access code is shared or compromised, an unauthorized person could use it to gain access to the home.

title: Guest identified through access patterns
description: Analysis of access code entry patterns (time, frequency) could identify the guest even without explicit identification.

title: Guest cannot deny access code entry
description: If the guest denies entering the access code, there may be no reliable way to prove or disprove their claim.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of household activity patterns
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written to the local event log could reveal sensitive information about household routines, presence, and activities, potentially exposing privacy if the log is accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Tampering with event log integrity
description: The local event log could be modified or deleted by unauthorized actors with physical or digital access, compromising the integrity of security records and potentially enabling denial of events.

title: Linkability of events to individuals
description: Sensor events could be linked to specific individuals or activities, enabling profiling of household members' behaviors and movements over time.

title: Identification of individuals from event data
description: If event metadata contains identifying information (timestamps, locations, device associations), individuals could be identified from the event log even without explicit personal data.

title: Video footage identifies individuals
description: Surveillance camera footage captured by the Home Hub can directly identify people in the home, including family members, visitors, and intruders.

title: Video data leakage during upload
description: Video clips may be intercepted or leaked during transmission from Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage if encryption is not properly implemented.

title: Unauthorized access to stored video footage
description: Cloud video storage may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, allowing third parties to view private surveillance footage without consent.

title: Linking video data to specific individuals
description: Video footage stored in the cloud can be linked to specific individuals, times, and locations, potentially revealing patterns of behavior.

title: Video data tampering
description: Stored video footage could be altered, modified, or deleted by unauthorized parties, compromising the integrity of the surveillance data.

title: Home Hub impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate the Home Hub to upload malicious or unauthorized video data to the cloud storage.

title: Privacy regulation non-compliance
description: Cloud video storage may not comply with privacy regulations like GDPR, potentially leading to legal and compliance issues.

title: Linkability of Motion Alert Data
description: The real-time motion alert transmitted from the Home Hub could be linked to a specific user's home and activity patterns, potentially enabling profiling of user behavior and presence at home.

title: Identifiability of Home Occupants
description: Motion alerts contain location and timing data that could reveal who is present at the home, potentially identifying specific occupants or their routines.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Motion Data
description: The mobile app backend could be compromised or accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of motion alert data to third parties.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The backend may collect and store more motion data than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Linkability of motion detection events to homeowner activities
description: The motion-detected notification could be linked to other data about the homeowner's activities, location patterns, or daily routines, potentially revealing behavioral patterns or presence at the property.
assumptions: The notification contains or can be correlated with timestamp and location data that could be linked to other data sources.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of motion detection notification
description: The notification could be intercepted, viewed by unauthorized parties, or leaked through the communication channel, revealing that motion was detected at the property.
assumptions: The notification transmission channel is not fully secured or could be compromised.

title: Excessive data in motion detection notification
description: The notification may contain more data than necessary (e.g., precise location, timestamp, camera feed) than required for the homeowner to be informed of motion detection.
assumptions: The notification includes metadata or additional information beyond what is needed for basic notification purposes.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about exact notification content and data minimization practices.

title: Unauthorized access to homeowner notifications
description: An unauthorized party could potentially access the homeowner's notification system and view motion detection alerts, compromising the homeowner's privacy regarding property monitoring.
assumptions: The notification system or device is accessible to unauthorized individuals.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with cloud vendor could potentially be linked to individual users through cross-referencing with other data sources or metadata, enabling re-identification risks.
assumptions: Vendor has access to additional data sources that could be correlated with the analytics data.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Cloud analytics vendor may share or sell the aggregated analytics data to third parties without proper authorization or user consent, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Vendor has business incentives to monetize or share data beyond the original agreement scope.

title: Inference of User Behavior Patterns
description: Even aggregated analytics may reveal sensitive behavioral patterns, preferences, or usage habits that could be used to profile users or infer sensitive information.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient detail to enable meaningful behavioral inference.

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Transmission
description: Analytics data could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during transmission between mobile app backend and cloud vendor, leading to inaccurate analytics or potential data manipulation.
assumptions: Transmission channel lacks adequate encryption or integrity verification mechanisms.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Sharing aggregated analytics with external vendor may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, or vendor due diligence are not in place.
assumptions: Vendor operations or data handling practices do not meet applicable regulatory requirements.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Video Content During Transmission
description: Video clip data transmitted from cloud storage to mobile app backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully encrypted or authentication is weak

title: Video Content Tampering During Transmission
description: Video clip data could be modified or corrupted during transmission from cloud storage to mobile app backend, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Transmission channel lacks integrity verification mechanisms

title: Video Content Reveals Homeowner Identity and Location
description: Video content retrieved by mobile app backend could reveal the identity, location, or activities of the homeowner, leading to identification risks.
assumptions: Video contains identifiable visual information about the homeowner or their property

title: Video Data Linked to Other Personal Information
description: Video clip data could be linked to other personal data about the homeowner (e.g., name, address, contact info) through metadata or cross-referencing.
assumptions: System stores or processes additional personal data that could be correlated with video content

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Playback
description: Unauthorized users could gain access to the video playback functionality through compromised mobile app backend credentials.
assumptions: Authentication and authorization controls are insufficient
